knott.name: Dr. Ron Knott
knott.role: Mathematician & computer scientist (formerly Dept. of Mathematics, University of Surrey); author and curator of Fibonacci Numbers, the Golden Section and the Golden String (1996–2025).

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.role: Author of the Elements; formalized division in extreme and mean ratio (II.11, VI.30), the golden 72°–72°–36° triangle and regular pentagon/15-gon (IV.10–16), and the icosahedron/dodecahedron (Book XIII).

fibonacci.name: Leonardo Pisano (Fibonacci)
fibonacci.role: Pisan mathematician whose Liber Abaci (1202) introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe and posed the monthly rabbit problem generating 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, …

pacioli.name: Luca Pacioli
pacioli.role: Franciscan friar and mathematician; authored De Divina Proportione (1509, illustrated by Leonardo da Vinci) cataloging thirteen geometric effects of the Golden Ratio across plane and solid figures.

kepler.name: Johannes Kepler
kepler.role: Astronomer and geometer; discovered the (1, √Φ, Φ) right triangle (1597 letter to Mästlin), observed F_{n+1}/F_n → Φ (1608), and studied the rhombic triacontahedron.

ptolemy.name: Claudius Ptolemy
ptolemy.role: Alexandrian astronomer-mathematician whose Almagest chord theorem (Book I.10) yields the pentagonal diagonal-to-side identity d = Φ s and exact trigonometric tables.

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras of Samos
pythagoras.role: Founder of the Pythagorean school; associated with the pentagram badge (ὑγίεια) and right-triangle quadrance additivity.

cassini.name: Giovanni Domenico Cassini
cassini.role: Italian-French astronomer and mathematician who presented F_{n-1} F_{n+1} - F_n^2 = (-1)^n to the Royal Academy of Sciences in 1680.

euler.name: Leonhard Euler
euler.role: Swiss mathematician whose Machin-type rational arctangent decompositions underpin the reciprocal Fibonacci telescoping series for π/4.

gauss.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
gauss.role: Proved at age 18 (30 March 1796; Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, 1801) that the regular 17-gon is constructible by straightedge and compass via nested quadratic radicals.

binet.name: Jacques Philippe Marie Binet
binet.role: French mathematician who published (1843) the closed-form power formula F_n = (Φ^n - (-φ)^n)/√5 previously known to Euler, Daniel Bernoulli, and de Moivre.

catalan.name: Eugène Charles Catalan
catalan.role: Belgian-French mathematician who generalized Cassini's identity to F_n^2 - F_{n-r} F_{n+r} = (-1)^{n-r} F_r^2 (1879).

lucas.name: Édouard Lucas
lucas.role: French number theorist who named the Fibonacci sequence, introduced the companion Lucas sequence L_n = Φ^n + (-φ)^n, and developed Fibonomial coefficients.

loyd.name: Sam Loyd & Sam Loyd Jr.
loyd.role: American puzzle pioneers who popularized both the 64 = 65 vanishing-square dissection and the 64 = 63 notched-rectangle dissection.

dudeney.name: Henry Ernest Dudeney
dudeney.role: English mathematical puzzle creator who analyzed generalized Fibonacci chessboard dissections for both +1 gap and -1 overlap paradoxes.

hurwitz.name: Adolf Hurwitz
hurwitz.role: German mathematician who proved (1891) that |α − p/q| < 1/(√5 q²) has infinitely many rational solutions for every irrational α, with √5 optimal specifically because of Φ.

thompson.name: D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson
thompson.role: Scottish biologist, mathematician, and classicist whose On Growth and Form (1917) analyzed Fibonacci phyllotaxis and gnomonic biological growth.

wythoff.name: Willem Abraham Wythoff
wythoff.role: Dutch mathematician who characterized cold positions of Wythoff's Nim (1907) as the complementary Beatty pairs (⌊nΦ⌋, ⌊nΦ^2⌋).

zeckendorf.name: Édouard Zeckendorf
zeckendorf.role: Belgian physician, army officer, and amateur mathematician who published the canonical non-consecutive Fibonacci representation theorem (1972, discovered c. 1939).

lehmer.name: Derrick Henry Lehmer
lehmer.role: American number theorist who posed (1936) the reciprocal Fibonacci arctangent series π/4 = ∑_{k=1}^∞ arctan(1/F_{2k+1}).

coxeter.name: Harold Scott MacDonald Coxeter
coxeter.role: Geometer whose Regular Polytopes and Introduction to Geometry unified 3D golden polyhedra, 5-cube compounds, and cylindrical phyllotaxis lattices.

penrose.name: Roger Penrose
penrose.role: Mathematical physicist and geometer who discovered the five-fold aperiodic P2 (kite & dart) and P3 (thick & thin golden rhomb) tilings in 1973–1974.

conway.name: John Horton Conway
conway.role: Mathematician who named Penrose's 'kite' and 'dart' prototiles and connected Fibonacci shift operations with Wythoff's array.

stolarsky.name: Kenneth B. Stolarsky
stolarsky.role: Number theorist who constructed the Stolarsky interspersion array (1977) via nearest-integer Golden Ratio rounding.

kimberling.name: Clark Kimberling
kimberling.role: Mathematician who formalized interspersion and dispersion arrays generalizing the Wythoff and Stolarsky arrays, and curated the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers (ETC).

bergman.name: George M. Bergman
bergman.role: Mathematician who discovered and published the base-Φ ('phigit') positional numeral system in 1957 at age 14.

wildberger.name: Norman J. Wildberger
wildberger.role: Creator of Rational Trigonometry (Divine Proportions, 2005), replacing transcendental distance and angle with exact algebraic quadrance and spread.
